name: United States
title: Free college in the USA for international students: need-blind schools and full scholarships
lede: American sticker prices are the highest in the world, but a small group of colleges admit international students without looking at their finances and then pay whatever the family cannot. Add Berea's no-tuition model and a few flagship graduate awards, and the USA becomes one of the most generous places to study.
description: How international students can study in the USA for free: need-blind colleges that meet full need, colleges with no application fee, Berea College, merit scholarships, Knight-Hennessy, Fulbright and Mastercard Foundation programmes.
card: A handful of colleges are need-blind for internationals and pay full need; graduate awards cover the rest.

sections.html: Need-blind means a college decides whether to admit you without considering whether you can pay. Meeting full need means that, once admitted, the college gives you enough grant aid to cover the gap between the cost of attendance and what your family can afford. Colleges that do both for international students are rare, and they are the best route to a free US degree. Read our full guide to US financial aid for international students.

On this board: Harvard, MIT, Yale, Princeton, Amherst, Dartmouth and Brown. Several now publish income thresholds below which families pay nothing: under $100,000 at Harvard, MIT and Yale, and up to $150,000 for most families at Princeton.

Duke and Colby meet the full need of the international students they admit, but consider financial need in admission. Vanderbilt offers full-tuition merit scholarships that international applicants can win, with a separate application due 1 December.

Berea College in Kentucky has charged no tuition since 1892. For admitted international students, aid covers 100% of tuition, housing, food and fees, and a compulsory campus job pays for personal costs. The international deadline is 30 November.

Selective US colleges usually charge $50 to $90 to apply: $50 at Vanderbilt, $75 at Amherst, $80 at Brown, and $85 at Dartmouth and Duke. Two colleges on this board charge nothing: Colby has no application fee for anyone, and Berea's application is free.

Harvard, MIT, Yale and Princeton waive their fee for applicants who cannot afford it, international applicants included. Ask for the waiver in the Common App (or in MIT's own application) instead of paying; MIT says asking has no effect on your chances.

Compare other countries in our guide to universities with no application fee.

For master's and doctoral study, look at Knight-Hennessy Scholars at Stanford (deadline 6 October 2026), the Fulbright Foreign Student Program (apply in your home country), and, for young Africans, the Mastercard Foundation programmes at UC Berkeley and Arizona State. Many US PhD programmes also fund admitted students through assistantships.

Undergraduate early deadlines fall on or around 1 November and regular deadlines in the first week of January. You will need school reports, teacher recommendations, essays, English-test results where required and financial aid forms such as the CSS Profile. Start a year ahead.

sections.h: Proof of funds and the I-20
sections.html: Before a college can issue the Form I-20 you need for an F-1 student visa, you must prove you can pay for your studies: tuition, fees and living costs for one academic year, or for the whole programme if it is shorter. Family bank statements, a sponsor's documents, financial aid letters and scholarship letters can all count. At colleges that meet full need, your aid award is part of that evidence.

On an F-1 visa you may work on campus up to 20 hours a week while school is in session, and full time in the breaks. Off-campus work needs separate authorisation. After graduating you can apply for up to 12 months of Optional Practical Training (OPT) in your field, and graduates of approved STEM degrees can extend it by 24 months with an employer enrolled in E-Verify.

faq.q: Which US colleges have no application fee for international students?
faq.a: Colby College charges no application fee to anyone, and Berea College's application is free. Harvard, MIT, Yale and Princeton waive their fee for applicants who cannot afford it, including international applicants.

faq.q: Can international students study in the US for free?
faq.a: Yes, at a few colleges: those that are need-blind or meet full need for international students can cover everything your family cannot pay, and Berea College charges no tuition.

faq.q: How much money do I need for a US student visa?
faq.a: Enough to cover one academic year of tuition, fees and living costs, as shown on your Form I-20. Scholarships and financial aid letters count.

faq.q: Can I work in the US after graduating?
faq.a: F-1 graduates can apply for up to 12 months of OPT, and STEM graduates can extend it by 24 months.
